clue.text: Print of ruined, disused lighthouse outside Knock

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit outside the knock, wrapping round it
something ruined is wrecked, so the remaining letters are knocked into a new order
read as dis-USE-d: the word use is dropped from the lighthouse

parts.note: a knock is a rap on a door

explanation.surface: An art print shows an abandoned lighthouse in ruins, standing beyond the village of Knock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disused' is read as dis-USE-d, dropping USE to leave LIGHTHO, which 'ruined' scrambles to LITHOGH. Knock is also an Irish village, which helps the scenic misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A lithograph is a print made from a flat stone or metal plate, so it is a kind of print.

clue.text: Part of plant insect recycled

indicators.note: cycled round, so the front letter of the insect goes round to the back

parts.note: a flea is a small jumping insect

explanation.surface: A gardener notes that an insect has been recycled into part of a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recycled' sends the F of FLEA round from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf is one of the green organs growing from a plant's stem, so it is a plant part.

clue.text: Stop supporting paper record of event logged digitally

indicators.note: in a down clue, the piece supporting sits underneath the other

parts.note: The Times is a British newspaper
to tamp is to stop up or plug a hole, as with a blast hole

explanation.surface: Someone stops backing a newspaper's record of an event that was logged on a computer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'supporting' puts TAMP below TIMES.
explanation.definitionFit: A timestamp is the date and time a computer attaches to an event as it is recorded.

clue.text: Overdose on wine after serving up more rum

indicators.note: in a down answer, the overdose sits on top of the wine
served up in a down clue means turned upward, so the word for wine is read from the bottom

parts.note: red is red wine

explanation.surface: A tale of someone overdosing on wine after it has been served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving up' turns RED into DER, placed under OD. Rum is an old British word for strange.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage rum means strange or peculiar, so more rum is stranger, which is odder.

clue.text: Congressman produced fake news, made comeback

parts.note: a member of the US House of Representatives is a Rep
someone who produced fake news lied

explanation.surface: A US congressman puts out fake news and so makes a political comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a comeback is to retort, to reply to a remark, so it matches replied.

clue.text: Saw Blackburn player perhaps going into lead

indicators.note: the footballer goes into the symbol for lead, which is split around him

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for lead
Blackburn Rovers is an English football club, so one of its players could be a Rover

explanation.surface: A wise saying about a Blackburn footballer taking the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' looks like the past tense of see, but it is the noun: an old saying. Blackburn Rovers is a football club in Lancashire.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old saying or maxim, which is what a proverb is.

clue.text: Like scorer of try, one going round to keep things moving

definitions.meaning: a rugby player scoring a try is carrying the ... down

definitions.text: one going round to keep things moving
definitions.meaning: a ... rolls round in a machine to reduce friction

explanation.surface: A rugby try-scorer is praised as a person who keeps the game flowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball bearing is a steel ball that rotates in a race so that moving parts turn freely.

clue.text: Cutting answer bringing up nothing good

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: nix is slang for nothing

explanation.surface: A cutting reply that achieves nothing good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bringing up' reverses NIX to XIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Axing something is chopping or cutting it, as in axing jobs from a budget.

clue.text: Given lager, drunk's making the most of the situation

definitions.text: making the most of the situation

indicators.note: the letters, like someone drunk on lager, stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone handed a lager makes the most of things by getting drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Leveraging means exploiting an advantage to the full, which is getting the best out of a situation.

clue.text: Sought to reform media

indicators.note: to reform is to reshape, so the letters are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Campaigners tried to reform the media.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sought' is the definition here, in the sense tried or aspired.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimed, as in aimed to do something, means tried or sought to do it.

clue.text: In favour of Ukrainian government's detaining of Russian composer

parts.note: pro means in favour of

indicators.note: the capital holds the word of inside it, like a detainee

parts.note: Kiev, the capital, stands for the Ukrainian government

explanation.surface: Someone backs a Ukrainian government holding a Russian composer.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital city stands for the government, as Westminster does for Britain's; 'detaining' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: Sergei Prokofiev was a 20th-century Russian composer, best known for Peter and the Wolf.

clue.text: Break into song — but you won't raise the roof in this kind of venue!

definitions.text: you won't raise the roof in this kind of venue!

parts.note: to break into something is to open it up
an air is a tune or song

explanation.surface: Singers bursting into song cannot lift the roof off a venue with no roof at all.
explanation.walkthrough: To raise the roof is to cheer very loudly; an open-air venue has no roof to raise.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-air venue is outdoors and roofless, so there is literally no roof for a loud crowd to raise.

clue.text: American in diner's ordered fish

indicators.note: the American is placed in the middle of the rearranged letters
put in order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive is read as the letters of diners

explanation.surface: An American in a diner orders fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges DINERS to SRDINE, and A goes 'in' after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: A sardine is a small oily fish of the herring family, often sold in tins.

clue.text: Keen sense of hearing catching ends of dying note

indicators.note: the ear catches the letters as they fall inside it

parts.note: the ear is the organ, and figuratively the sense, of hearing

indicators.note: the last letter of each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A keen ear catches the fading end of a dying note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ends of' takes G and E, the last letters of 'dying' and 'note', and EAR catches them.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and keen are synonyms, both meaning enthusiastic and impatient to do something.

clue.text: One having two pints outside home before start of extended period of isolation

indicators.note: the home comes before the next letter
the quart is outside, round the one

parts.note: a quart is two pints
an means one, as in a single thing
in means at home

indicators.note: the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone downing two pints away from home before a long period stuck alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having … outside' signals the insertion; 'extended' looks part of the definition, but only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarantine is a time of enforced separation to stop a disease spreading.

clue.text: Without a scratch — not hard when opponent is this?

indicators.note: not here means the letter for hard is left out

parts.note: someone without a scratch is unharmed
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A fighter escapes without a scratch, which is no hard feat if the other side has no weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question: you would get off without a scratch when the opponent is weaponless.
explanation.definitionFit: An opponent without weapons is the one most likely to leave a fighter uninjured.

clue.text: Two odours in timeshare possibly equine

indicators.note: the two odours share a letter T, so it appears once rather than twice

parts.note: must is a musty smell and tang is a sharp smell

explanation.surface: Two smells in a timeshare apartment that might be horsey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'timeshare' is read as T-share: MUST and TANG overlap on their shared T.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a wild horse of the American plains, so it is one example of an equine.

clue.text: See 6
I clean out wound and protect from disease

indicators.note: wound as in twisted, the past tense of wind, so the letters are twisted round

explanation.surface: A medic cleans out a wound and protects the patient against infection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound' looks like an injury but is the twisting of wind, the anagram signal; it rearranges CLEAN OUT after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: To inoculate is to vaccinate, giving immunity against an infection.

clue.text: Reformed prisoner, with term discharged, enlists

indicators.note: a reformed prisoner is changed, so the letters are formed anew
the term, or end letter, of the word prisoner is let go

explanation.surface: A former inmate, sentence served and released, signs up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'term' means end, so the last letter R of PRISONER goes, leaving PRISONE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To rope someone in is to persuade them to take part, which is enlisting them.

clue.text: Towards the top, it's on either side of right and left, and it smells

indicators.note: the reversed letters sit on both sides of the letter for right
in a down answer, heading upward means the words are read from the bottom

parts.note: the letters of the two words it's and on

explanation.surface: Something high up on the face, flanking the right and left, does the smelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Towards the top' reverses ITSON to NOSTI, which sits 'either side of' R; L follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A nostril is an opening of the nose, the organ by which a person smells.

clue.text: Illegally take web address over, cracking digital access code

indicators.note: the address breaks open the code and sits within it

parts.note: a PIN is a personal identification number
a URL is the address of a web page
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A hacker steals by taking over a web address and cracking a PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To purloin is to steal, which is taking something unlawfully.

clue.text: Settle around Skye, perhaps to make cloth

indicators.note: the word for settle goes around the island

parts.note: to settle a bill is to pay it
Skye is an island in the Scottish Hebrides, so an example of an isle

explanation.surface: Someone settles on Skye to weave cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Paisley is fabric printed with a swirling teardrop pattern named after the Scottish town.

clue.text: 'Assassin in Japan' covers it

indicators.note: the phrase in quotes holds the answer inside it, wrapping it up

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style claim that the phrase 'assassin in Japan' sums up the word.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted phrase both defines the answer and contains it, across 'assassiN IN JApan'.
explanation.definitionFit: A ninja was a Japanese warrior trained in stealth, hired as a spy and assassin.

clue.text: Between east and west coast cities we find a species of antelope

indicators.note: the letter a sits between the two city abbreviations

parts.note: NY is New York on the US east coast and LA is Los Angeles on the west coast

explanation.surface: A wildlife spotter finds a rare antelope somewhere between New York and Los Angeles.
explanation.definitionFit: The nyala is a spiral-horned southern African antelope.

clue.text: Chinese man's best friend has university pursuing his revolutionary 'How to Zoom for Beginners'

indicators.note: the university chases, coming after the other letters
a revolutionary overturns the order, so these letters are rearranged
the beginnings, the first letters, of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A Chinese man's dog owns a revolutionary self-help guide on video calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges HIS to SHI; 'for Beginners' picks HTZ from 'How to Zoom'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogs are called man's best friend; the shih tzu is a small long-haired toy breed from China.

clue.text: All express disapproval of appeal being overturned

parts.note: tut is the clicking sound of disapproval

indicators.note: in a down answer, overturned means the word reads upward

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Everyone clicks their tongues at a court appeal that has been overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being overturned' turns IT to TI. Tutti is a musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutti is Italian for all and in music marks a passage for the whole orchestra.

clue.text: Sickly — to conserve energy, adjust diet

indicators.note: the word for sickly conserves, keeping hold of the energy inside it

parts.note: wan means pale and sickly-looking
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A sickly person is told to save energy by changing what they eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To wean a baby is to move it off milk onto solid food, a change of diet.

clue.text: During summer month, Russian flower's opening

parts.note: in means during, as in in August
Aug is the abbreviation for August
the Ural is a river in Russia; a flower here is something that flows

explanation.surface: In midsummer a Russian flower opens its petals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' means a thing that flows, a river, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Inaugural means first in a series, as in an inaugural address that opens a term.

clue.text: Reverse farm vehicle bearing scrap

indicators.note: to reverse is to back up, so the vehicle's letters are read backwards

parts.note: a cart is a farm vehicle
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: A driver backs a farm cart while carrying a load of scrap metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace is a tiny amount, a scrap, as in not a trace of evidence.

clue.text: Something to be taken late in the morning

parts.note: ex means former, so late as in the late president
a.m. stands for the morning hours

explanation.surface: A medicine to be swallowed late in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something to be taken' suggests a pill, but exams are taken too.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam is a test that a student sits or takes.

clue.text: Member of Doves joins Mud — disc released to be hit

indicators.note: the pigeon joins on behind the mud

parts.note: clay is a sticky mud
doves belong to the pigeon family

explanation.surface: A band member from Doves joins the group Mud, and a record is released to become a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Doves and Mud are both British bands; the disc is a target not a record.
explanation.definitionFit: A clay pigeon is the disc flung into the air as a target in clay shooting.
